title: Work continuity: how sessions share one memory

subject.lede: Today the rules and decisions for a feature live inside one long chat, and every summary loses some. The plan writes them into a private notebook on your laptop, never in the team's repositories, so any session, old, new, any worktree, starts from the same page. Your own backup carries it to a new laptop, and helper agents get a short card instead of a copy of the chat.

context.purpose: Start any session on a feature and have it already know which PR does what, what is on hold and what was decided, without you repeating it.
context.why_now: In one recent session you repeated the same rules about {{m1}}, and forks used {{fork_share}} of the tokens.
in_scope: Saving decisions, holds and conventions in a private notebook on your laptop
Briefing every new session at start-up
Telling an open session what changed
A lock so two sessions do not fix one PR
Warning before forking a summarised session
out_of_scope: Anything teammates can see in a repository

terms.means: A private notebook for one feature, kept as files on your laptop, that every session reads and adds notes to.
One feature family: all the PRs that belong together.
terms.example: Album comments: backend, frontend and settings PRs.

terms.means: A one-page summary of the record, handed to a session when it starts.
A note that blocks a push or PR until it is released.
A lock that says which session is working on a PR right now.
A helper agent that starts with a copy of the whole conversation.
What happens when a chat gets too long: the start is replaced by a short summary, and details are lost.
A small script the plugin runs at set moments: session start, each prompt, before a push.
Your claude-setup tool, which copies the notebook to your private backup and restores it on a new laptop.
terms.example: Nothing manual on a new Mac.

terms.means: The last note a session has seen, so it can be told what is new.
One step of the rollout; each must pass before the next is built.

outline.title: session start, then each prompt, then each push

lines.code: workstream = lookup(host/owner/repo from git remote, branch)
on each prompt: inject 'since you last looked' if there are newer notes
before git push / gh pr: refuse if the PR is held or claimed by another session
before a fork after a summary: warn and offer a brief

diagrams.title: The rollout: each phase must pass before the next is built
diagrams.source:
flowchart LR
  P0["Phase 0: backup PR merged + cloud prompt check"] --> P1["Phase 1: brief, notes, fork warning"]
  P1 --> M{"brief fits the budget and forks drop on your next feature?"}
  M -- yes --> P2["Phase 2: what-changed notes, holds and claims enforced"]
  M -- no --> STOP["Stop: drop it before building more"]
  P2 --> P3["Phase 3: decision queue, only one-way doors reach you"]
diagrams.caption: Each phase is built only after the one before it passes on a real feature. Phase one works on a single laptop even before the backup change merges.

diagrams.title: Who talks to whom
diagrams.source:
flowchart LR
  A["Session A"] --> H["Plugin hooks"]
  B["Session B: any terminal, worktree or config dir"] --> H
  H -->|read, add one file| W[("Private notebook on your laptop")]
  H -->|lock file| K[("Claim locks, this laptop")]
  H -->|check holds| P["git push / gh pr"]
  W -.->|your own backup| CS[("claude-setup, private")]
  CS -.->|restore| W2[("Notebook on another laptop")]
diagrams.caption: Sessions never talk to each other or to the team's repository. They read and write one private folder, and your own backup carries it to other laptops.

options.label: Private files on your laptop, carried by your own backup
pros: Restored on a new laptop with no manual step
cons: Cloud sessions only get the brief in their first prompt
Two laptops agree after each syncs

options.label: A dedicated private repository the plugin pushes to
cons: The plugin would have to push

options.label: A hidden ref in each project repository
Claude Code's own memory
cons: Each worktree and config dir sees a different copy

decision.deciding_factor: It is the only option that keeps everything out of the team's repositories without the plugin pushing, and your existing backup already restores it on a new laptop.
decision.revisit_when: Cloud sessions become your main way of working.

checks.q: The chat was just summarised. Where will Session A put the next fix?
checks.answer: It guesses, because the rule was in the part of the chat that got summarised away.

checks.q: Session B is brand new. Does it know where fixes go?
checks.answer: Yes: the brief from the record tells it at start-up.

checks.q: Both asked at once and Session A won. What happens to Session B's request?
checks.answer: Refused: the lock file already exists, and only one create can succeed.

nodes.label: Session B (new: another terminal, worktree or background)

fork_per.basis: 8.0 billion fork tokens / 327 fork agents (PRD section 9c)

brief_per.basis: 1.7 billion tokens / 365 general-purpose agents; different tasks, rough

lease.basis: PRD Q4 recommendation, renewed on each push or event

e-waves.anchor: Every task in a wave runs at once

scenarios.title: Today: the rules live only in the chat, so a summary loses them

steps.t: You tell Session A where fixes go
steps.d: Example: fixes to the comment API go on the backend branch.
do: fixes go on the backend branch

steps.t: Weeks of work pile up in the same chat
steps.d: One session in your review carried {{prompts}} of your prompts.

steps.t: The chat gets too long and is summarised
steps.d: The summary keeps the gist and drops details like which branch owns which fix. That session was summarised {{compactions}} times.

steps.t: Session A puts a fix on the wrong branch
steps.d: It no longer knows the rule, so it guesses.

steps.t: You repeat the rule, again
steps.d: This happened about {{m1}} in that session.
do: again: fixes go on the backend branch

steps.t: A forked helper copies the whole chat
steps.d: A fork starts with the entire conversation, about {{fork_per}} each. Forks were {{fork_share}} of all tokens.

scenarios.title: With the work record: the rule is written down in a private notebook every session reads

steps.t: The rule is also saved as a note in the work record
steps.d: Think of a hospital chart: whoever is on shift reads it and adds a note. The note is one new file in a private folder on your laptop, not in the chat and not in the team's repository.
do: append note: fixes go on the backend branch

steps.t: The chat is summarised, as before
steps.d: Chat memory still loses the detail. The notebook does not.

steps.t: Session B starts in another terminal or worktree
steps.d: It does not need Session A's id: the hook finds the feature from the repository and branch.

steps.t: The hook reads the notebook from disk
steps.d: Local files only, no network, so it never hits the start-up cut-off of {{hook_timeout}}.

steps.t: Session B gets a short brief at start-up
steps.d: Goal, which PR does what, merge order, holds, decisions, conventions, and a line saying it is private: never quote it in commits or PR text.
do: brief: fixes go on the backend branch, PR #3 on hold

steps.t: Your own backup carries the notebook to a new laptop
steps.d: Your backup tool copies the folder to your private backup and restores it on a new Mac. The team's repositories never see it.

steps.t: Benchmark: the brief answers what the chat forgot
steps.d: A fresh session got {{brief_correct}} of {{questions}} with the brief and {{none_correct}} without, over {{runs}}. It was cheaper ({{brief_cost}} against {{none_cost}}) and faster ({{brief_secs}} against {{none_secs}}).

scenarios.title: An old session is still open while you give a new session new instructions

steps.t: You tell Session B: do not push PR #3 yet
steps.d: Session B saves it as a hold in the record.

steps.t: Session A sees the new note on disk
steps.d: Session A never talks to Session B; both read and write the same private folder.

steps.t: Session A's next prompt starts with what changed
steps.d: A hook adds a line before your prompt: since you last looked, PR #3 is on hold.
do: since you last looked: PR #3 is on hold

steps.t: Session A tries to push PR #3 anyway
steps.d: Before any push or PR, the hook re-checks the record.

steps.t: The push is refused
Teammates see none of this
steps.d: No file, branch, setting or commit text in the repository comes from the notebook.

scenarios.title: Two sessions try to fix the same PR at the same moment

steps.t: Both sessions ask for the lock on PR #1
steps.d: Each tries to create the same lock file; the operating system lets only one create succeed.

steps.t: Session A's request lands first and wins
Session B is refused, because the lock already exists
steps.d: Two winners are impossible: the create is atomic.

steps.t: Session B waits, works read-only, or takes over on purpose
steps.d: Taking over is explicit and logged. A claim expires after about {{lease}} so a crashed session cannot block forever.

scenarios.title: Parallel helpers stay fast, but get a task card instead of a copy of the chat

steps.t: Today: a fork helper gets the whole conversation
steps.d: Like photocopying the whole notebook for every helper: about {{fork_per}} each.

steps.t: Instead: a fresh helper gets a one-page task card
steps.d: Goal, files it owns, its worktree, the verify command and the brief: about {{brief_per}} each.

steps.t: Helpers still run side by side
steps.d: Independent tasks run at once, each in its own worktree. Nothing about the parallelism changes.

steps.t: After a summary, a fork gets a warning
steps.d: Phase one adds a hook: forking from a summarised session warns and offers a brief.
do: warning: this session was summarised, send a brief instead
